title: Katie Zacharia Set to Exit as White House Press Secretary After Barely a Week
snippet: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is stepping down after less than a week on the job following intense public scrutiny over her legal credentials.
content:
WASHINGTON — White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is departing her post after less than a week on the job, following a turbulent few days dominated by relentless questions regarding her professional background and legal credentials.

Multiple news outlets reported Friday afternoon that Zacharia is transitioning out of her role, positioning her to become the shortest-tenured White House press secretary in American history. Speaking on the South Lawn, President Donald Trump signaled that her time in the Briefing Room was coming to an end, lamenting the fierce media coverage she faced during her first days in office.

Credential Controversy Unravels Brief Tenure

Zacharia was appointed on Oct. 9 to replace former press secretary Karoline Leavitt, who left the administration in August. In his initial announcement, Trump touted Zacharia as a brilliant "attorney" and staunch MAGA supporter. However, press scrutiny quickly focused on her background after reports revealed she had failed the California bar exam after graduating from Pepperdine University School of Law and never retook it.

While public records show she was never licensed to practice law in any U.S. state or the District of Columbia, Zacharia defended her past use of the title "lawyer" in television interviews. She argued that holding a law degree permitted her to provide legal analysis, though legal ethics experts noted that non-licensed graduates cannot hold themselves out as licensed attorneys or corporate general counsel. The non-profit watchdog Campaign for Accountability subsequently filed a complaint with the California bar regarding her claims.

Trump Points to Media Scrutiny

Addressing reporters on Friday before traveling to a campaign event in Georgia, Trump stated that he encouraged Zacharia to evaluate whether the role was worth the personal toll.

"I told her, 'I think you're better off being happy and I don't think you could ever be happy in this job,'" Trump told reporters, adding that she was being "brutalized by the media." While Trump stopped short of saying he directly fired her, senior White House officials acknowledged her impending departure.

Zacharia, a 42-year-old mother of four and former conservative commentator, conducted only one formal press briefing during her brief stint, which lasted 15 minutes on Tuesday. The White House has not yet announced a successor for the position.
